correctness.rationale: The arrow ideal is the radical: it is nilpotent and the quotient is a product of copies of the field. A full unit squaring to 1 has semisimple coordinates 1 on every field extension, but this argument does not eliminate possible infinitesimal diagonal coordinates in the full scheme. In 1+J write u=u1+u2 by path length. Then (1+u)^2=1+u1^2; each length-two path (a,b) is a distinct basis vector with coefficient c_a c_b, including when ab and ba exist or when a=b is a loop. The defining ideal therefore consists of these monomials, leaving p2 path coordinates free. Adding the loop variables to the ideal kills the genuine loop nilpotents (no linear monomial lies in the original quadratic ideal), and the remaining edge ideal is the intersection of the primes killing the complement of each maximal independent support. This proves the scheme and component statements over any characteristic-two field. A compatible set of nonloop arrows has disjoint source and target sets, hence lies in a directed cut; every cut is compatible. Doubling undirected edges gives the undirected cut size, with p2=sum deg(v)^2, so the dimension computes MaxCut. Assigning nonzero values on a support and arbitrary path coordinates gives the exact finite-field census. The fourth power is trivial and a composable pair supplies a nonzero square because path coordinates are separate, giving the exponent criterion. For an oriented cycle, trace of the two-state matrix [[1,q-1],[1,0]] counts compatible cyclic words, with initial traces 2 and 1 and the stated recurrence; the directed triangle gives 32 and 640.
residual_risks: The raw arithmetic replay is finite and does not test nilpotents or all fields; these are established by the monomial-ideal proof. The full unit group is covered only at field-valued points, not scheme-theoretically. The NP-hardness premise is standard simple unweighted MaxCut; cited full text was unavailable.

evidence: Graphical groups allow arbitrary simple conflicts, not loop squares. The cited module varieties and odd-characteristic algebra anti-involutions concern other objects.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Put loops to zero and choose a single product equation per conflict edge. Then on field points the normalized count is exactly q^{p2-|E(Gamma_Q)|} times the graphical-group count for Gamma_Q; the graphical equations likewise give the same reduced arrangement up to an affine factor. This is genuine coverage of the support enumeration, not a coincidence of polynomials. It does not give the original scheme's nonzero loop nilpotents or the dimension interpretation on Q. value.rationale: The normalized involution scheme is a natural unit-group invariant, and passing to finite-field counts alone hides loop nilpotents. The all-multiquiver scheme classification distinguishes these features and relates its largest component to a natural optimization problem on the original quiver, not just to a computation on sample graphs. The cut complexity and general reducedness criterion supply value beyond the overlapping support census and cycle specialization.
residual_risks: No classification of conjugacy classes, all unit-group scheme nilpotents, or longer truncation is claimed.
